newsitem.title: USA: 4,500 Ohio health care workers go on strike.
newsitem.headline: 4,500 Ohio health care workers go on strike.

text.p: More than 4,000 doctors, nurses, social workers and other state-employed members of the Service Employees International Union went on a one-day strike Tuesday morning after a breakdown in negotiations.
Pickets were up around the state at state-run prisons, hospitals, mental health centres and nursing homes as the union's first 24-hour strike took hold at 6:45 a.m. EDT, a union spokeswoman said.
"There's good turnout at the picket lines and no problems," Shannon Howington of District Local 1199 in Columbus said.
Union leaders said members had authorised the "non-traditional" strike of one day per two-week pay period, but that could escalate to a longer walkout if no progress is made. No talks were scheduled.
A contract expired Aug. 2 covering 4,500 state workers that included various categories of health care and prison workers such as parole counsellors and dieticians.
Negotiations broke off July 31 at the state's instigation, the union said, just after government negotiators cut their previous salary offer to the union.

The union said the state sought to reduce wages by up to 8 percent to employees with more than 10 years of service and other rollbacks. It also unilaterally implemented the new contract terms this week, the union said.
"The state's refusal to even allow a mediator to participate demonstrates once again the intransigence of the governor's position," Local 1199 union president Dave Regan said in a statement.
"We expect that we won't have many problems, that we'll be able to provide services," a spokesman for Ohio Gov. George Voinovich's collective bargaining office said.
The spokesman said the union had rejected an independent fact-finder's conclusion that longevity pay for the workers was probably too high when compared to other state employees.
It was the first strike by Ohio employees since collective bargaining was permitted under a 1984 state law.
